```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

Enterotypes are clusters of gut microbiome samples. Whether a given sample
belongs to one enterotype or another can depend on **which other samples are
clustered with it**: the clinical composition of the cohort (ERP) and its size
(ERPM). This package quantifies that dependence for every sample, on any
abundance table.

The vignette runs on a simulated table so that it builds without cohort data.
Iteration counts are kept tiny; the paper used 500 iterations per condition.

```{r data}
library(enterotyperobustness)
X <- simulate_enterotype_counts(n = 80)
markers <- c(bacteroides = "Bacteroides", prevotella = "Prevotella")
richness <- attr(X, "diversity")
```

## ERP: perturb the composition

An **anchor set** is held fixed and clustered, at every iteration, with a random
draw of **complementary** samples from a pool. Each anchor sample gets one label
per iteration; the fraction of iterations giving each label is its assignment
frequency.

```{r erp}
anchors <- rownames(X)[1:40]
pool    <- rownames(X)[41:80]
res <- erp(X, anchors, pool, n_complementary = 12, n_iter = 5,
           marker_features = markers, diversity = richness,
           keep_fits = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
res
freq <- assignment_frequency(res)
head(freq[anchors, ])
head(robustness(res))
```

Two ERP conditions of the same anchors (different pools) give a
samples x conditions label matrix, from which core (same enterotype in every
condition) and variable samples follow:

```{r core}
res2 <- erp(X, anchors, pool[1:20], n_complementary = 12, n_iter = 5,
            marker_features = markers, diversity = richness,
            keep_fits = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)
lab <- labels_by_condition(list(cond1 = res, cond2 = res2))
table(core_variable(lab)$status)
```

Because the same anchors appear in every condition, comparisons between
conditions must be paired: `paired_entropy_test()` (Friedman with post hoc
tests), `cochran_q_test()` and `anchor_permutation_test()` for the labels, and
`mixed_entropy_model()` / `multinomial_mixed_test()` for mixed-effects versions.

## ERPM: perturb the size

`erpm()` draws stratified fractions of a cohort and tracks how the assignment
of each sample stabilises as the fraction grows.

```{r erpm}
classes <- stats::setNames(c("A", "B")[attr(X, "group") %% 2 + 1], rownames(X))
resm <- erpm(X, classes, fractions = c(0.5, 0.9), n_iter = 3,
             marker_features = markers, diversity = richness, verbose = FALSE)
resm
rb <- robustness(resm$results[["Q0.90"]])
bootstrap_ci(rb$robustness, R = 200)
```

## Annotation and reproduction of the published runs

Components are named after the fit, never before. `annotate = "rank"` is the
published heuristic (highest mean *Bacteroides* = Bact2, second = Bact1, highest
*Prevotella* = Prevotella, the rest = Ruminococcus); `annotate = "match"` matches
component centroids to `reference_centroids()` of a reference fit by
Jensen-Shannon distance. Annotation checks are returned as flags in
`res$flags`, never as errors.

With the defaults (`iteration_seeds = 1:n_iter`, `dmm_seed = 314`,
`integerise = "trunc"`) and the sample IDs in the original order, `erp()` and
`erpm()` reproduce the draws and fits of the 2022 analyses of the paper. Note
that `DirichletMultinomial::dmn()` itself is not run-to-run deterministic on
multimodal data (a few percent of fits can reach a different optimum), so
iteration-level identity is not guaranteed; aggregates are stable.
